Hi Maria — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a concise package and a diagram set to start. High-level notes up front so your reviewers have context:

1) Control-plane: logically isolated control plane for Dedicated and Private modes. No cross-customer configuration state is stored in the tenant-facing control path; shared control services are restricted to management VLANs and audited via centralized logging.

2) FenceBridge mapping: when customers choose bridging (VPC peering / private connectivity), we establish explicit demarcation nodes ("fencebridge" proxies) per region that terminate customer network traffic and apply tenant-scoped firewall policies. These nodes are the only egress points for customer compute to the public internet in a given region unless an air-gapped option is selected.

3) KMS and key custody: by default Redwood manages envelope keys in our KMS for hosted deployments; for Dedicated/Private we provide options: customer-managed keys (via customer KMS integration), or tenant-specific keys stored in a dedicated KMS partition. We label keys by tenancy and rotate at customer-configured intervals.

4) Evidence index: attached zip contains a matrix mapping SIG/CaiQ/SOC2 claims to the artifacts we can provide (design diagrams, config snapshots, audit extracts). I highlighted artifacts that require an NDA or higher access tier.

Next steps: can you confirm whether Atlas expects customer-managed KMS for this intake, and whether you need the diagram changelog and an attestation signed by an engineering lead? If so, we'll generate the change list and run the attestation process.

- [Attachment: redwood-evidence-bundle_Atlas-Reqs.zip (ZIP) — index and supporting artifacts]

Maria / Markus — adding a few technical clarifications to help your SOC/SIG reviewers:

- IP addressing: tenant compute runs in customer-scoped subnets; our fencebridge proxies perform NAT-only for outbound flows to public endpoints unless customer requests passthrough. We publish the NAT egress pool ranges in the evidence bundle.

- VLAN & VRF: For Dedicated deployments we allocate dedicated VRFs per customer. For Private (VPC-based) deployments, routing separation is enforced via route-table segregation and security-groups; we avoid shared L2 bridging.

- Control plane endpoints: management/control-plane APIs live on an internal-only network and authenticate via mTLS with service identity. Logs from control-plane interactions are shipped to an immutable audit log (append-only) in the evidence bundle.

- KMS: the diagrams include two options (hosted KMS with key partitions, or customer KMS integration via external key references). If you select customer KMS, we will show the key handshake and a sample CMK ARN in the diagrams.

Attachments referenced:
- [Attachment: segmentation-claim-index.csv (CSV) — claim -> artifact mapping]
- [Attachment: kms-boundary-diagrams.png (PNG) — visuals for key custody options]

If helpful, I can extract the exact SOC 2 control IDs (CC6/CC7/CC8 equivalents) and map them in-line next. Would you like that or do you prefer us to keep the artifact bundle first and follow with control mappings?

—Kimberly Park
